Act as release orchestrator for this repository. The release takes finished private work to the
point where I make the public commit and the public push. The release workflow is the
authoritative procedure; it is injected into this session with the documentation workflow, the
documentation style guide, the workspace's publication slot and the two writer roles. A release's
first step merges the integration branch into the plan's branch in this worktree, and a hotfix skips
it because it runs in the integration worktree. Step 2 is the export:
`python AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PUBLISHING/export.py`.

This session runs in the released plan's worktree, or in the integration worktree for a hotfix; the
merge into the integration branch happens in that branch's own worktree, as step 7 says. A hotfix
has no plan: there is no plan's `docs-pass.md` list and no plan to close. Your inputs are the
uncommitted public changes after a fresh export, the open plan's
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/docs-pass.md` list (delete each item once resolved) and this
conversation.

Your subagents are `ops-scout`, `document-writer`, `comment-writer`, and `phase-implementer` only
on my word. Any other subagent requires my explicit permission. Spawn every one in the background.
Ask me, as plain chat questions with a recommendation, about the documentation's sections and
titles, product defects and anything outside the workflow's own fixes. Never edit `AGENTS.md` or
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/` unless I say so, except deleting resolved `docs-pass.md` items and the plan
closure I approve.

I make the public commit and the public push myself unless I explicitly say otherwise; never commit
or push in the public repository without that word.

Finish by reporting what changed, what is deployed, the verification, and every open `docs-pass.md`
item with its reason. Then I check, commit and push.

Release coordination: plan-c merges first. Merge plan-c into main. Keep plan-c open until plan-a's release, which merges last: any docs-pass item on a file the other plans also change stays for that release, so record its owner in docs-pass.md. Report the merge and the open items, then stop.

This is a test run of the toy project. No export, public checkout or deployment applies: publish.md is authoritative and the toy publishes nothing, so skip those steps. Merge in the integration worktree and resolve every conflict by the shared designs in AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/ and the plans' done contracts, then run the fast gate and the rendered-image gate in main. The root README and the documentation pages belong to the documentation hotfix after the last release, so leave them out unless a merge breaks a statement in them. Ask me only for product decisions and anything the workflow cannot settle.

# Output Plan

> **Status:** scoped forward plan, revised 2026-11-24 on branch `plan-c`.
> **Scope:** how the program is run and what it writes: the PNG writer, the command line and the
> progress line (`docs/requirements.md` items 11 to 13).
> **Out of scope:** materials, sampling, jitter and scattering (the materials plan); shapes, hit
> data and bounding boxes (the geometry plan).
> **Target:** a correct, small hobby raytracer. Every phase here is product work; no phase is an
> experiment.
>
> **How to use this plan:** expand exactly one phase into an implementation-grade phase from
> current code before coding. Discuss and edit phase boundaries here first.

## Phase status

| Phase | Title | Status | Gate level | Depends on | Phase file | Exit state | Move-on gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PNG writer and command line | done | standard | - | `done/C1-survey-remediation.md` | the program writes a real PNG at the chosen size, path and format from the command line | fast gate green, the written PNG opens, PPM still writes |
| C2 | (merged into C1) | not applicable | - | - | - | - | - |
| C3 | Progress line | done | standard | C1 | `done/C3-progress-line.md` | rendering shows the share of rows done on standard error | fast gate green, progress observed, image unchanged |
| Z1r | Shared render seam resolution | done | minimal | C1 + C3 | `done/Z1r-shared-render-seam.md` | the shared design is recorded and plan-c's render seam and acceptance render are confirmed against it | documentation gate green, acceptance render observed |
| Z1 | Closing survey and user acceptance | done | minimal | C1 + C3 | `done/Z1-closing-survey.md` | the closing survey note is written and the user accepts the result | the user accepts |

C2 was folded into C1 so that PPM never becomes unreachable code and the format choice exists in
the same change that makes `render.png` the default.

## How to implement this plan

1. Read `docs/requirements.md` items 11 to 13, the README, `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` and
   the code the selected phase touches before detailing it.
2. Never invent a name, signature, path or option. If something the phase names does not exist,
   stop and report drift.
3. One phase at a time. Commits whenever useful, no squashing, never on `main`.
4. Product code: no dependency, no hardcoded second path, no `allow(dead_code)` to paper over
   plumbing. `Cargo.toml` stays dependency-free.
5. Run the fast gate in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md`, plus the rendered-image conditional
   gate whenever the render loop or the output format changes.
6. Fail loudly: a bad option, a bad value or an unwritable output path reports and exits non-zero;
   no silent fallback format or path.
7. Update the README in the phase that makes its usage line wrong. A genuine deferral to the release
   goes in `docs-pass.md`.

## Binding design rules

1. No dependency. The PNG is built from stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with CRC-32 per chunk
   and Adler-32 in the zlib trailer computed in the writer itself. No crate, no build script, no
   bundled compressor.
2. The PNG writer lives in `src/png.rs`. The PPM writer stays `write_ppm` in `src/main.rs`. `main`
   resolves the options and calls exactly one of them; there is no third output path.
3. Options resolve once into one set of settings before rendering. Defaults are 400 by 200, 16
   samples, `render.png`, and the format from the output file's extension. An explicit `--format`
   wins over the extension. An unknown option, a value that does not parse, an unrecognised format
   or an unrecognised output extension prints a usage line and exits non-zero.
4. `--samples` is accepted and validated here and passed into the render loop as a parameter; each
   pixel averages that many rays. The rays are not jittered yet, because scattering belongs to the
   materials plan, so today every sample count produces the same bytes at `samples` times the cost.
   That is the honest intermediate state: this plan must not add jitter or scattering, and the
   materials plan fills it in. The render signature is the seam the materials plan consumes.
5. Standard output stays clean: the image goes only to the output file and the progress line only to
   standard error. No image bytes on stdout.
6. Rendering stays reproducible: the same options give the same bytes. No new randomness, no time,
   no environment-dependent output.
7. Single-threaded, no `unsafe`, one concept per module, shared types in the module that defines the
   concept. Every module starts with a `//!` line.
8. Docs follow the change: the README run example is updated by the phase that makes it wrong. The
   rendered-image fallback sentence in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` stays until the release,
   because that file is shared by every worktree and the sentence is still true where this plan's
   command line has not landed; its removal is recorded in `docs-pass.md`.

## Starting state

- `src/main.rs` renders a fixed 200 by 100 through `render(width, height)` and writes ASCII PPM
  (P3, maximum 255) to standard output through `write_ppm(out, width, height, pixels)`; `to_byte`
  clamps and scales a channel. There is no option parsing and `std::env::args` is unused.
- Two tests in `src/main.rs` pin the centre pixel and the top row from `render(200, 100)`.
- `README.md` shows `cargo run > image.ppm`. `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` carries the same
  fallback ("until the command-line phase lands, `cargo run --release > render.ppm`").
- There is no `src/png.rs` and `Cargo.toml` has no dependency.
- Known gaps: no PNG writer, no command line, no progress line, and the rendered size is 200 by 100
  rather than the required 400 by 200.

What later phases inherit:

- `render` gains the sample count; `write_ppm` stays reachable through `--format ppm`.
- The output file is the only place the image goes; stdout carries nothing but what the user asks
  for.
- One resolved settings value per render; later phases add behaviour behind it, not a second parse.

## Scoped phases

### C1 - PNG writer and command line

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** none (the first phase).
**Scope:** the program stops writing PPM to standard output and instead resolves a small set of
command-line options and writes the image to a file as PNG or PPM. This is the phase that makes the
output side of the product match requirements 11 and 12.
**Expected gate level:** standard.

**Starting state / reason:**
- The image only exists as PPM on stdout; there is no file, no size choice and no PNG.
- Requirement 11 wants a dependency-free PNG, requirement 12 the five options and their defaults.
- PPM must stay available, which is exactly why the format choice lands together with the PNG
  writer: switching the default to `render.png` on its own would leave `write_ppm` uncalled.

**Likely areas to touch:**
- `src/png.rs` - new module with the writer.
- `src/main.rs` - option parsing, the resolved settings, the render signature, `main`.
- `README.md` - the run example.
- `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` - read only here: it is shared by every worktree, and its
  fallback sentence is deferred to the release (`docs-pass.md`).
- `docs/requirements.md` - only if the change contradicts a stated behaviour; otherwise leave it.

**TODOs:**
1. Add `src/png.rs`: a writer taking the width, the height, the pixels and a `Write`, producing the
   signature, `IHDR` (8-bit RGB, no interlace), one `IDAT` with zlib-wrapped stored deflate blocks
   of at most 65535 bytes, `IEND`, a CRC-32 per chunk, a filter byte of 0 per scanline and the
   Adler-32 trailer.
2. Parse the command line by hand into one resolved settings value: `--width`, `--height`,
   `--samples`, `--output <path>`, `--format png|ppm`, with the required defaults, explicit format
   winning over the extension, and a usage line plus non-zero exit for anything bad.
3. Make `main` render at the chosen size with the chosen sample count and write the chosen format to
   the chosen path, reporting an unwritable path instead of panicking.
4. Give `render` the sample count and average that many rays per pixel; no jitter.
5. Update the README run example. Leave `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md` untouched; its fallback
   sentence is deferred to the release.
6. Adapt the two existing render tests to the new signature and add at most three new test
   functions covering the public behaviour: the binary writes a file that is a valid PNG whose
   pixels match the PPM rendering of the same scene; a bad option or bad value prints usage and
   exits non-zero; the format follows the output extension and an explicit `--format` wins.

**Must not:**
- Add a dependency, a build script or any real deflate compression.
- Delete `write_ppm` or bypass it with a second PPM path.
- Silence unused plumbing with `allow(dead_code)`; the sample count must reach `render` because it is
  used there, not because it is parked.
- Add jitter, scattering, gamma or any materials work; the materials plan owns those.
- Change the scene contents or the camera.
- Test the exact usage wording or private parse helpers; test the public behaviour through the
  binary.
- Leave the README run example stale, or edit the shared `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md`.

**Verification shape:**
- Fast gate: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `git diff --check`.
- Rendered-image gate (this phase owns it): a small render through the real command line in both
  formats, the PNG opened and looked at, the PPM compared with the same-size render.
- Documentation reread of the changed README lines plus `git diff --check`.

**Exit:** `cargo run` writes `render.png`; size, sample count, output path and format are honoured;
PPM still writes through `--format ppm`; a bad option prints usage and exits non-zero.
**Move-on gate:** fast gate green, the written PNG opens and looks right, PPM still writes,
work committed.

### C3 - Progress line

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** C1 (it consumes the render loop and the resolved settings C1 leaves).
**Scope:** while rendering, the program reports the share of rows done on standard error, updating
one line instead of printing a new one per row.
**Expected gate level:** standard - the phase changes runtime output, so the minimal level does not
apply.

**Starting state / reason:**
- Rendering is silent; at 400 by 200 with 16 samples it takes long enough that silence looks like a
  hang.

**Likely areas to touch:**
- `src/main.rs` - the render loop and its caller.

**TODOs:**
1. Report the row share on standard error as rows finish, overwriting one line.
2. Leave the finished line terminated so later output is not glued onto it.
3. Keep the image bytes exactly what they were for the same options.

**Must not:**
- Write progress to standard output or into the image file.
- Add a timing, throttling or verbosity option; the requirements ask for one line.
- Test the exact progress text or its refresh cadence.
- Change pixels, sampling or the scene.

**Verification shape:**
- Fast gate.
- Rendered-image gate (this phase owns it): a small render with the progress line observed on
  standard error, and the same image bytes as before the change for identical options.
- No separate acceptance test beyond the agent-run checks.

**Exit:** a render shows its row share on standard error while it runs.
**Move-on gate:** fast gate green, progress observed, image unchanged, work committed.

### Z1r - Shared render seam resolution

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** C1 + C3 and the shared design `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A3+plan-c-Z1.md`.
**Scope:** record the shared render design in the plan, confirm plan-c's landed `render` seam and
frozen C1/C3 contracts against it, and re-run plan-c's acceptance render. No product code, test,
README or `docs/` change.
**Expected gate level:** minimal.

**Starting state / reason:**

## Target shape of the shared code

`src/hittable.rs` holds one `HitRecord`, not `Copy`:

```rust
pub struct HitRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub point: Vec3,
    /// Always faces against the incoming ray (requirement 7).
    pub normal: Vec3,
    pub front_face: bool,
    pub u: f64,
    pub v: f64,
    pub material: Rc<dyn Material>,
}
```

One constructor:

```rust
pub fn new(ray: &Ray, t: f64, point: Vec3, outward_normal: Vec3, u: f64, v: f64, material: Rc<dyn Material>) -> Self
```

It sets `front_face = ray.direction.dot(outward_normal) < 0.0`, then `normal = outward_normal` when
`front_face`, otherwise `-outward_normal`.

`HittableList::hit` reads the nearest distance through a borrow:
`let limit = nearest.as_ref().map_or(t_max, |hit| hit.t);`.

Every shape holds an `Rc<dyn Material>` and passes it to `HitRecord::new`.

Spheres derive `(u, v)` identically on both branches, from the outward normal, so the sphere merge is
textual:

```
let outward_normal = (point - self.center) / self.radius;
let theta = (-outward_normal.y).acos();
let phi = (-outward_normal.z).atan2(outward_normal.x) + PI;
let u = phi / (2.0 * PI);
let v = theta / PI;
```

The merged `render` in `src/main.rs` takes plan-a's scene, camera, generator and `ray_colour`, and
plan-c's progress write:

```rust
/// Every pixel's colour, row by row from the top, each pixel averaging `samples` jittered rays, with
/// the share of finished rows reported on standard error.
fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::new(SEED);
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width * height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let mut colour = Colour::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                let u = (column as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / width as f64;
                let v = (row as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / height as f64;
                colour = colour + ray_colour(&camera.ray(u, v), &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(colour / samples as f64);
        }
        let done = height - row;
        eprint!("\r{}%", done * 100 / height);
    }
    eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

### Local environment

The project has no runtime configuration and no secrets. Cargo and its tools live in
`~/.cargo/bin`; when `cargo` is not on `PATH`, call `~/.cargo/bin/cargo`.

### Fast phase gate

For code changes, run named tests covering touched behavior and regressions, then:

```bash
cargo build
cargo test
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
git diff --check
```

Documentation-only changes require changed-file reread plus `git diff --check`. Prose a change
writes or edits follows `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/BUILDING/DOCUMENTATION-STYLE-GUIDE.md`. Tests follow
REPO-RULES §3a; the receipt states functions added/deleted.

### Experiment gate

This project has no experiments.

### Conditional gates

| Gate             | Run when                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rendered image   | The render loop, a material, the camera or the output format changed     |
| Agent generation | `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/SUBAGENTS/**` or agent model assignment changed      |

## 1. What this repo is

A small raytracer in Rust 2021 with no dependencies beyond the standard library. It renders one
fixed scene to an image file. `src/main.rs` holds the scene, the render loop, the output and the
command line; each other module in `src/` holds one concept. There is no experiment directory.

---

## 2. Hard invariants: never violate

These bind product code. Experiments follow only the binding list in `REPO-RULES.md` §0a.

1. No dependency in `Cargo.toml`. Everything, the PNG writer included, uses only the standard
   library.
2. Rendering is reproducible: all randomness comes from `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value, so
   the same options give the same bytes.
3. Single-threaded rendering; no `unsafe`.

If a task seems to require violating an invariant, stop and ask.

---

- One concept per module in `src/`; shared types live in the module that defines the concept

- Scene objects are `Box<dyn Hittable>`; materials are shared as `Rc<dyn Material>`. Avoid

# Requirements

A small raytracer with no dependencies beyond the Rust standard library. It renders one fixed scene
and writes the image to a file. Every render is reproducible: the same options give the same bytes.

## Materials

1. Every object has a material. A ray that hits an object scatters by that material and the colour
   is the material's attenuation times the colour the scattered ray sees, up to a bounce limit of
   50; a ray that reaches the limit is black.
2. Diffuse material scatters in a random direction around the surface normal and attenuates by its
   albedo.
3. Metal material reflects about the normal, blurred by a fuzz factor in 0..=1, and attenuates by
   its albedo. A reflection that points into the surface is absorbed.
4. Glass material refracts by its refractive index using Snell's law, reflects on total internal
   reflection, and chooses reflection by Schlick's approximation otherwise. It does not attenuate.
5. Each pixel averages a configurable number of samples (default 16), jittered inside the pixel,
   with gamma 2 correction on output.
6. All randomness comes from the seeded generator in `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value.

## Geometry

7. Every hit records whether the ray hit the front face, and the normal always points against the
   ray.
8. Every hit records texture coordinates `(u, v)` in 0..=1: spheres by latitude and longitude,
   planes by the hit point's position along two axes in the plane, modulo 1, and triangles by their
   barycentric coordinates.
9. The scene can hold infinite planes (a point and a normal) and triangles (three vertices).
10. Every object reports an axis-aligned bounding box, and the scene list tests a ray against an
    object's box before the object. An infinite plane has no box and is always tested.

## Output and command line

11. The image is written as PNG, with no external crate: one IDAT chunk holding zlib data made of
    stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with correct CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums. PPM stays
    available.
12. The command line takes `--width`, `--height`, `--samples`, `--output <path>` and
    `--format png|ppm`. The defaults are 400 by 200, 16 samples, `render.png` and the format from the
    output file's extension. An unknown option or a bad value prints a usage line and exits with a
    non-zero status.
13. While rendering, a progress line on standard error shows the share of rows done.

## Quality

14. `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
